Khalilur Rahman with Khalilur Rahman (Helal) and Mohammad Zafar Ali Khan, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate with Syed Mokaddas Ali, Advocates—For the opposite party Nos. 1, 2, 4-9, 11-16, 3(a)-3(e) and 10.

4. That RS Khatian No. 2629/21 appertaining to RS plot No. 13119 and 13109 comprising an area of 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.16 acre were recorded in the names of Ahammad Khalil and Ahammad Kabir to the extent of 4 annas and 16 gandas each and the remaining 6 annas 8 gandas were recorded in the name of Hafizur Rahman, who by amicable settlement with other co-sharers lived in 0.6 acre homestead portion and same was recorded in his name. In this way plaintiff Nos. 1-16 inherited through their predecessor Aminulla 0.07 1/4 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/15, .04 from RS Khatian No. 2926/16, 0.34 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/17, 0.17 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/18 and 0.6 acre from RS Khatian No, 2926/21 totaling an area of 0.68 1/4 acre of land. The plaintiff Nos.1-16 have got their right, title interest and possession in the schedule properties. The defendant Nos. 3-16 are co-sharers of the disputed khatians for which they have been impleaded as defendants to avoid defect of parties. Since the names of other defendants are wrongly recorded in the BS khatian, they have also been impleaded in the suit. It was further stated in the plaint that the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, Md Abdul Monayem filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for Khas possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 against three sons of Aminulla, Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah. They appeared in the said suit and filed joint written statement stating that they have no knowledge about Other Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit no notice was served upon the defendant and the decree was collusive, no auction sale was held in Decree Execution Case on 27-1-1954 and there was no commission report by the Advocate Commissioner and delivery of possession of the Property on 11-4-1957 through court. Ultimately the above suit was dismissed on compromise. In fact Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal, void, inoperative and without jurisdiction. The plaintiff tried to compromise the matter with the defendants through the arbitration of local Commissioner, but the defendants did not appear. Subsequently, the defendants with a view to harass the plaintiffs filed Non-GR No. 468 of 1986 under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Criminal Case No. 254 of 1990, and Panchlaish GR Case No. 33(8) of 1990 in local Police Station against the plaintiffs. The cause of action arose on 19-9-1991 when the defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them. Subsequently, by amending the plaint the plaintiff prayed for a declaration that the decree dated 31-7-1952 passed by the Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and auction sale held on 27-9-1954 in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 are null and void, ineffective, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for partition. 

 5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the said suit by filing joint written statement denying all the materials allegation made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, there is no cause of action and the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the same is not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and khas possession and further the suit is barred by waiver, Estoppel and acquiescence, the principle of res-judicata, defect of parties and also barred by limitation. The positive case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are that the predecessor of the defendants are that, Abdul Monayem obtained the preliminary decree in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 on 31-7-1952 passed by the Munsif Fifth Court, Chittagong against Moulvi Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the land described in the suit schedule alongwith other property. Accordingly, final decree was prepared on 5-3-1953 in which the decree-holder got saham of 0.342/7 acre in his share from RS plot No. 13104 and 13108. Thereafter in respect of cost of the suit he filed Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 in which he purchased 0.06 acre of land in auction sale from RS plot No. 13109 and took delivery of possession through court on 11-4-1957. Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was permitted to live in RS plot No. 13108 temporarily, but after his death his three sons Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah refused to surrendered possession to the predecessor of the defendants and for which he filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for eviction. Ultimately the suit was dismissed in terms of solenama on 16-8-1969. 

 7. The plaintiffs have field the instant suit without paying required court fee on proper valuation of the suit land. These defendant along with other co-sharers are in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years by paying rents regularly, receiving rent-receipts. Hence they have got the absolute right, title, interest and possession over the suit land which the Plaintiffs have got no right to deny. The defendants have filed criminal case No. 523 of 1990 against the plaintiffs for theft of their fish from the pond of RS plot 13105 perhaps in turn of which they might have filed the present test suit which deserves to be dismissed. In fact the plaintiffs are well aware of the Final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and the auction sale which have been purchased by the predecessor of the defendants and all other deeds also. It is utter surprise to mentioned that where the plaintiffs have already admitted in their plaint about the sole decree dated 16-8-1969 passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 how they can file the instant suit. Their predecessor-in-interest have specifically admitted the conditions save and except the possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 they would never claim their previously sold out properties of all other khatians to the predecessor of the defendants. As per sole decree the predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name correctly in BS khatian Nos. 693 and 695 which have finally been published in his name. After death, his heirs and subsequent heirs transferred 0.39 acre of land from BS plot Nos. 13252 and 13253 to Ashekane Awlia Abdul Monayem High School by registered Deed of Gift No. 7542 dated 1.6-12-1987 and delivered possession, which is within the schedule described in the plaint. Having been well aware of all these facts and circumstances, the plaintiffs intentionally did not make these defendants as parties to the suit. Now the defendants along with their transfers are, in fact, is in possession of their respective lands about which the plaintiffs are not at all entitled to claim any decree and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Defendant no. 24 contested the suit by filing a separate written statement wherein he also stated all the facts of final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and reiterated the same facts as stated in the written statement filed on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1-2. It was further stated that Abdul Monayem executed registered Wasiatnama No. 34 dated 31-12-1974 in favour of sons and daughters relinquishing all his properties including the land of the schedule khatians of the suit. After his death, his daughter Mst Numahar Begum having been in possession of her properties died leaving 2 sons 5 daughters and husband as her legal heirs. Her husband Md Ismail Hossain Seraji executed another registered Wasiatnama No. 25 dated 19-7-1995 in favour of his two sons Md Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam. Thereafter Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam having acquired the property by way of Wasiatnama from father, by way of inheritance from their mother and 2 daughter of Abdul Monayem Tahera Parvin and Farida Yasmin having from mother by way of inheritance jointly transferred by kabala No. 4340 dated 5-8-1996 to this defendant from RS plot No. 13104 an area of 8 gandas 2 karas 2 kranti and 1 1/2 danta Ithiti land and handed over possession to this defendant. This defendant having delivery of possession of his purchased land constructed boundary walls around the land and pucca gate where he engraved his name and has been possessing peacefully since purchase. He was not aware of the suit and he was not made party to the suit. Having been informed from reliable source he appeared with a prayer to be added as party in the suit and was made party on his prayer. All the claims of the plaintiffs are false. They cannot deny the decree and decree execution case. This defendant is in possession of his purchased property by paying rent, cesses and receiving rent receipts. The suit is hopelessly barred by the principles of waiver, estoppel Acquiescence and also barred by limitation and res-judicata and is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The learned Joint District Judge upon consideration of materials evidence on record by his judgment dated 25-11-2008 decreed the suit. Against the said decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 in the Court District Judge, Chittagong and in due course appeal was transferred to the Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong. In Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 plaintiff filed an application on 13-6-2010 calling for the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 of Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 of the same court describing the papers and documents in the said application and same was rejected by the appellate court by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010. Ultimately, the learned Additional District Judge after hearing the parties, dismissed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 12. During pendency of the revisional application before this court, the petitioner filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 10-3-2013 for additional evidence stating the facts that the record of the Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 were called for in the present Other Class Suit No. 137 of 2001 and the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was transmitted to the trial court but record of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 could not be transmitted as it was found missing at the relevant time. But due to bonafide Mistake of the learned Advocate for the defendants as well as the trial court the relevant order of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was not exhibited. On the basis of such bonafide mistake, both the courts below erroneously found that the defendants did not take steps to prove the service of summons of Other Class Suit No. 39 of 1950 which was duly served upon the defendants. But on scrutinizing the order sheet of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, it appears that the defendant No. 1 Aminulla, the predecessor of the present plaintiffs was appeared in that suit and filed written statement on 22-2-1951 (order No.8) It also transpired from the order sheet of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 that the defendant (present plaintiff) appeared in that title suit and filed written statement and ultimately the suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn upon. It is pertinent to mentioned here that those documents were submitted by the plaintiffs in the appellate court but the appellate court below did not consider those documents as additional evidence. It was further stated that the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 are now before this hon'ble court and the petitioners on the advice of their learned Advocate collected certified copy of entire order sheet of Title Suit 53 of 1968 and written statement filed by defendants dated 10-3-1969. From those documents it will be crystal clear that summons were duly served upon the defendants in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and they have contested the said suit by filing written statements in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 respectively. It is also stated that in paragraph No. 2 of the plaint of the present suit the plaintiffs admitted that they appeared and filed written statements in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968. Since the plaintiffs are admitting the facts of their appearance in the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, which can be easily taken as additional evidence, as admitted facts need not be proved. 

 14. It is also denied that the decree holder Abdul Munayem gave 0.7 acre land to Aminullah for residing there temporary as licensee. It was further denied that Tajul Huda and his two brothers appeared and filed written statement on 10-3-1969 or on any other date in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 filed by Abdul Munayem. It is also denied that they filed a compromise petition on 7-8-1969 or any on other date and on the basis of said compromise petition suit was decreed. It was further stated that defendants had ample opportunities to exhibit the order sheet of Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 and both the courts below have given their findings on the decree passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1950, the Execution Case arising there from and on Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and hence the petitioners are not entitled to adduce additional evidence before the revisional court to patch up the weak part of their case which is not permissible under Order XII, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 15. Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr Khalilur Rahman(Helal) and Mr Mohammad Zafar Ali Khan, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the Defendant-petitioners. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners firstly, submits that the present suit was filed on 28-9-1991 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, and the plaintiffs had knowledge about filing of earlier Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which they have admitted in paragraph no. 2 of the plaint of the present suit. Since the present suit is filed long after 23 years from their knowledge, same is hopelessly barred by limitation. Secondly, Mr Khalil, submits that in respect of suit property, Abdul Munayem, father of the defendant nos. 1-2 filed Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 against the predecessors of the plaintiffs Aminullah who contested the said partition suit by filing written statement and ultimately preliminary and final decree was passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. Thereafter, the predecessors of the defendant again filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Aminullah who appeared and contested the Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement on 10-3-1969 and the said suit was decreed on compromise on 7-8-1969. Thirdly, learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit on the basis of korfa lease of their predecessors Aminullah and RS khatian was published in the name of their predecessor but they, failed to file any lease deed as such korfa lease and record of right does not create any title in the suit land. So, after passing of the final decree in a Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and compromise decree dated 7-8-1969 between the parties, and for the same self suit land, the present second suit is barred under the principles of res-judicata and not maintainable. Since the trail court failed to frame any issue in the present suit, whether the suit is barred by res-judicata and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Fourthly, the learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs has miserably failed to prove that fraud was committed in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Fifthly, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents. Sixthly, he submits that the plaintiff failed to established their title in the suit land, so they cannot challenge the title deeds of the defendants, who acquired title through the process of law. He lastly submits that both the courts below totally failed to consider the evidence, both oral and documentary and misread and non-considered the materials evidence on record and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Accordingly, the learned Advocate prayed that the rule should be made absolute. 

 17. On the other hand, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate submits that the suit is not barred by limitation because of the fact that the previous suit being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 filed by Abdul Munayam, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the present suit and the defendants Aminullah, predecessors of the present plaintiffs are not aware about the final decree passed in that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that no summons were served upon the defendants in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the said decree was obtained by practicing fraud, then auction sale held in other Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 were not effective and thus the suit is not barred by limitation and same are not binding upon the plaintiffs. In support of his submission he referred two decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 and 19 DLR (SC) 433, He further submits that the lower appellate court concurred with the findings of the trial court that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, thus the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title and partition is not barred by limitation. 

 He next submits that the defendants have failed to prove that the predecessor of the plaintiffs signed the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 which was affirmed by the appellate court. Therefore, the present suit is not barred by the principles of res-judicata and waiver. He also submits that the trial court found that the RS record prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during the period from 1924 to 1930 in Chittagong region same has presumptive value and the defendants did not challenge the same in any court of law. The predecessors of the plaintiffs-Aminuddin being korfa lessee and his successors continued in possession for more than 12 years and on the basis of the RS khatian they acquired title in the suit land. In this respect he placed reliance two decisions reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287 and 54 DLR (AD) 173. He then submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the decree in the Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 was void and defendants did not try to prove by sufficient evidence that the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 was actually executed by the three sons of Aminullah and therefore the defendants did not acquire any title by the said deeds, further the defendants did not appear in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement and compromise petition have been filed fraudulently by the plaintiffs of that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that the judgment and decree in the earlier partition suit are void, in-operative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Therefore, the present partition suit filed by the plaintiffs is quite maintainable and it is not necessary to have a separate decree for cancellation of the registered two deeds of the defendants. He further submits that both the courts below in consideration of the evidence, found that the deeds through which the defendants claimed title did not confer any title or possession on the defendants and gave cogent reasons in support of their findings and the courts had jurisdiction to consider whether the deeds conferred title or possession on the defendants even though some of those were 30 years old documents and the genuineness of such documents may be challenged and there is no misreading or nonconsideration of the material evidence by the courts below and the defendants are not entitled to challenge those findings. In this connection he refers the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 199. He also submits that the trial court found that the defendants claimed that Abdus Sabur is the owner of land described in the first schedule to the plaint, and in that case the onus is upon the defendant to prove the claim of ownership of Abdus Sabur but they did not file any documents in support of the ownership of Abdus Sabur. DW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that he did not know about any deed showing title of Abdus Sabur. Moreover the document dated 19-6-1895 shows that in that deed ten gandas of land stating Moghi dags were mentioned. But in the written statement the corresponding CS and RS dags had not been mentioned. The defendants did not adduce any documentary or oral evidence to show that the land mentioned in the above deed dated 19-6-1895 and the lands described in the schedule to the plaint are the same land. He also submits that the RS khatian have got presumptive value relating to title in the Chittagong region and the RS record was prepared in Chittagong region from the years 1924 to 1930. After settlement with Aminulla, Abul Bashar and Ithairul Bashar have no title in the land settled with Aminulla. Since the korfa settlement was coupled with possession, the defendants are not entitled to challenge the settlement of Aminulla after 12 years from the time of preparation of RS khatian. He further submits that the defendants fails to prove that Aminulla the predecessor of the plaintiff are in permissive possession of some land was not prove either in the earlier suit or in the present suit. So, the auction was not effective and hence the defendants did not acquire any,title in the land allegedly sold in auction. He finally submits that the application regarding the additional evidence as provided under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure prescribed that the need for additional evidence must be felt by the court itself. This provision of law is clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to fill up the omission. In this respect he referred to a decision reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220 and accordingly prayed for discharged of the Rule. 

 21. It further appears that earlier the suit land was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, which was filed by the predecessor of the present defendants against the predecessor of the present plaintiffs, Aminulla and others and got a decree. In support of their claim defendants exhibited the preliminary decree (Exhibit-Ka), final decree with Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit-kha), certified copy of the order sheet of original Execution Case No. 18 of 1953, Sale Certificate dated 8-4-1954 (Exhibit-Gha), certificate of delivery of possession dated 11-4-1957 (Exhibit-Ga) and kabala No. 3139 dated 5-6-1951 in favour of defendant No. 1.  But both the courts below failed to consider those documents of the defendants and erroneously found that by the said documents the defendants, present petitioners did not get any decree in the said suit. 

 22. It also appears that the predecessor of the present defendant filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the present plaintiffs and in that title suit defendant appeared and filed written statement and said suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn. To prove such facts the present defendants filed the application for compromise (Exhibit-Ja) and the sole decree (Exhibit-Ja(1) respectively, wherefrom it is evident that three sons of Aminulla executed the said solenama, but both the courts below failed to consider such vital aspect of the case and erroneously found that the defendants could not prove the said facts. It further transpires that the defendants filed an applications before the appellate court on 13-6-2010 for calling for the records of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, Title Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. The appellate court heard this application and rejected the same by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010 on the ground that— “আপীলকারী বিবাদীপক্ষে আনীত দরখাস্তটি অনাবশ্যক বিধায় আপাতত না মঞ্জুর করা হইল, তবে অত্র মোকদ্দমার আপীল শুনানীঅন্তে উক্ত দরখাস্তের বিষয়বস্তু বিবেচনাযোগ্য। 

 26. The learned Advocate for the defendants petitioners strenuously argued that the High Court Division conferred wide power in order to do justice in a case and it shows that in the instant case the appellate court failed to exhibits the aforesaid vital documents although the same was also filed before the appellate court but those documents were not considered at the time of hearing of the appeal. After consideration and appreciation of the materials and evidence on record it appears that the documents and papers filed by the defendants-petitioners are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the suit. It is, however, felt that ends of justice will be meet if both the parties should be given opportunity to prove their case by filing those documents in appellate court. In this connection reference is made to the case of Sunil Krishna Banki vs Kailash Chandra Saha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220. Since the court below totally misread and non-considered the Exhibits namely, Exhibit Nos. Ka to Umo, Exhibit Nos. Ja and J(1) and also did not call for the record of the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which is very much material to consider that whether the present defendants, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 obtain any decree fraudulently against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs. The opposite parties has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 137 of 2001 seeking, firstly prayed for declaration that both preliminary and the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and also the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal collusive and fraudulent, Secondly, the BS khatian No. 693 and 695 are wrong and baseless and also for partition of total 0.90 acres land claiming entire 0.64 1/4 acres which was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-2, Md Abdul Monayem was the plaintiff and predecessors of the present plaintiffs Aminullah was the defendant. 

 27. On going through the materials on record it is apparent that the heirs of the defendant of the earlier suit were all out to deprive the plaintiff of the said suit of the fruit of the decree and as last resort has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 on 28-9-1991 after 41 years of the first suit and 23 years of the second suit seeking the relief primarily by way ul setting aside the decrees that were passed in those two suits under the shadow of the relief seeking separate saham in respect of the schedule land. It is seen from the materials on record and admitted by the plaintiffs of the present suit that the land which was the subject matter of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 has also been made subject matter of present Other Suit No, 92 of 1991. 

 28. It is not disputed from the side of the plaintiffs that relief sought for in Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 relates to seeking set aside the decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 but the courts below failed to frame any issue whether the decisions made in the former suits operates as res-judicata in the present suit. 

 30. It appears that in respect of the suit land preliminary and final decree was passed on 11-8-1953 in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the defendants took possession of 34 2/7 acres of their saham on 20-6-1956 though court in Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. Thus after passing of the final decree in the said partition suit between the same parties, the second suit filed by the plaintiffs after 41 years is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. So, the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 is not applicable in the present case. In the present suit, the plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove that the decree obtained fraudulently in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Further, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents.
